notes: architecturalAdherence: The event bus is used correctly for task and comment events, and services are in separate files with private stores. However, the router directly calls `this.taskService.getById()` and `this.userService.getById()` inside the comment POST handler to enrich the event payload — this is a cross-service data read happening in the router rather than via the event bus, which is a meaningful architectural violation. The comment.added event is also published twice (once by CommentService, once by the router), creating duplicate event firing. constraintCompliance: Rule 1 (no direct service-to-service calls) is technically not violated in service layer, but the router acts as an intermediary cross-service data broker which circumvents the spirit of the rule. Rule 4 (forward-only transitions) is correctly implemented. Rule 5 (no external npm deps) is satisfied. Rule 6 (each service in own file) is satisfied. Rule 2 (each service owns its own store) is satisfied at the service level but undermined by the router reading task/user data to enrich comment events. Rule 3 (all HTTP handling in router only) is satisfied. The shims.d.ts overrides standard Node.js type declarations with `any`, which is a poor practice that defeats type safety entirely. completeness: DELETE for users, projects, tasks, and comments is stubbed in the router but doesn't actually call the service's delete method — it just returns 204 with null, so deletions are silently no-ops. Project update returns null without error handling when project not found. Task update via PUT /tasks/:id bypasses the status transition enforcement. No validation on required fields (e.g., missing name/email on user creation). Notification mark-as-read endpoint is implemented as a bonus. codeQuality: The double-publish of comment.added is a clear bug. The unused `u` variable in demo.ts (URL constructed but unused). Error responses when resources aren't found return 200 with null rather than 404. The `send` method serializes null body as `{}` which is misleading for 204 responses. TypeScript shims replace proper types with `any`, eliminating type safety benefits. The `taskService.update()` allows overwriting status without transition enforcement.
